Stamp Duty Land Tax - Residential property rates. You usually pay Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) on increasing portions of the property price when you buy residential property, for example a house or flat. The amount you pay depends on:. • when you bought the property. • how much you paid for it. • whether you’re eligible for relief or an exemption. Rates for a single property. You pay SDLT at these rates if, after buying the property, it is the only residential property you own. You will usually pay 5% on top of these rates if you own another residential property. Rates from 1 April 2025. Property or lease premium or transfer value SDLT rate. Up to £125,000 Zero. The next £125,000 (the portion from £125,001 to £250,000) 2%. The next £675,000 (the portion from £250,001 to £925,000) 5%. The next £575,000 (the portion from £925,001 to £1.5 million) 10%. The remaining amount (the portion above £1.5 million) 12%. Example. In April 2025 you buy a house for £295,000. The SDLT you owe will be calculated as follows:. • 0% on the first £125,000 = £0. • 2% on the second £125,000 = £2,500. • 5% on the final £45,000 = £2,250. • total SDLT = £4,750. 4 BEDROOM EXTENDED DETACHED FAMILY HOME. Situated in a popular and established residential location in Erdington, this attractive dormer bungalow offers particularly versatile accommodation, making it an excellent purchase for a variety of buyers. The property occupies a particularly desirable position along a private, unadopted and tree-lined road, offering a peaceful setting with a distinctly rural feel, almost reminiscent of a country lane. With no through traffic or pedestrian access for non-residents, the road enjoys an exceptionally quiet and secluded atmosphere, making it one of the most peaceful locations in the Erdington area. The property is approached via a paved front garden with a gated entrance and benefits from an area of off-road parking situated opposite the front entrance, which forms part of the property's ownership. The front lounge is a good-sized reception room featuring a decorative fireplace, while there are two ground-floor bedrooms, including a rear bedroom with wood-effect flooring and an adjoining snug area. The property is also well placed for access to the A38, providing convenient road links into Birmingham city centre and the wider motorway network. A spacious and versatile dormer bungalow offering a great deal of accommodation, useful outside space and the considerable attraction of an exceptionally peaceful, tree-lined private road setting, all within a convenient Erdington location. Offering generous and versatile accommodation, this property is ideally suited for family living or those seeking a property in a desirable part of Cornwall. The property also presents an excellent opportunity for buyers looking for a potentially straight-forward purchase. The accommodation comprises of a sitting room, dining area, separate kitchen, conservatory and a garage on the ground floor along with three bedrooms and a bathroom on the first floor. Colroger Close is situated within the popular and well established village of Mullion - one of the largest and most sought-after villages on the beautiful Lizard Peninsula in South Cornwall. Offering a wonderful balance of village convenience, community atmosphere and access to the spectacular Cornish coastline, Mullion is an excellent location for those looking to enjoy a relaxed coastal lifestyle. The village itself offers a good range of everyday amenities, including local shops, convenience stores, cafés, traditional Public Houses, restaurants and independent businesses. There are also primary and secondary schooling facilities, a health centre and pharmacy together with a variety of community groups and recreational activities. A particular attraction of the area is its beautiful surrounding coastline, with miles of scenic coastal walks and an abundance of picturesque beaches and secluded coves close by. Mullion Cove is a charming historic harbour, cared for by the National Trust, nestled beneath rugged cliffs and offering wonderful coastal scenery. Nearby Polurrian Cove and Poldhu Cove are particularly popular, with sandy beaches, opportunities for surfing, swimming and coastal walks along the renowned South West Coast Path. For a wider range of retail, leisure and commercial facilities, the nearby market town of Helston is approximately five miles distant, offering supermarkets, high street retailers, restaurants, leisure facilities and further schooling options. The location also provides a convenient base for exploring the wider Lizard Peninsula, including its picturesque villages, unspoilt countryside and renowned beauty spots. Combining excellent village amenities with easy access to some of Cornwall's finest beaches and coastal scenery, Mullion remains a particularly desirable location for families, retirees and those looking to embrace the very best of coastal living. SITUATION AND DESCRIPTION Occupying a truly exceptional waterfront position in the heart of the highly sought-after village of Bere Ferrers, this fascinating three-bedroom period home enjoys superb, uninterrupted views across the River Tavy towards the far banks. Rich in character and local history, the property combines wonderfully generous accommodation with a setting that is difficult to rival. Believed to date back more than 200 years in part, the property was originally three separate cottages, with the three original entrances still identifiable on an old photograph of the property – two positioned to the front and a third to the side, accessed from the road. For many years it played an important role within village life as the local shop and Post Office, before subsequently being converted to create the spacious and comfortable single home seen today. Its history remains very much part of its charm, with exposed beams, stonework, fireplaces and other period details found throughout. The accommodation is particularly generous, extending to approximately 1,791 sq ft, with three substantial reception rooms providing a great deal of versatility. The main sitting room is an impressive space, measuring approximately 19'7" x 14'4", with a characterful exposed stone wall and fireplace housing a wood-burning stove creating an attractive focal point. The fireplace also retains its original Cloam oven, a particularly interesting reminder of the property's age and history. From here, the property's wonderful position beside the river can be fully appreciated, with the outlook across the water providing an ever-changing backdrop. The dining room is another excellent-sized reception space and continues the character of the house, again benefiting from a wood-burning stove and exposed overhead beams. A further living room provides a third generous reception room, making the ground floor exceptionally flexible for entertaining, family life or those requiring a separate study or snug. The kitchen is positioned alongside the dining room and is fitted with a range of units and work surfaces. Completing the ground-floor accommodation is a useful shower room. Upstairs, the generous proportions continue with three well-sized bedrooms. The two principal bedrooms are particularly spacious, while the third is also a comfortable double room. Several rooms enjoy the property's remarkable outlook, taking full advantage of its position overlooking the river and surrounding landscape. A family bathroom completes the first-floor accommodation. Outside, immediately to the rear of the property is a small enclosed courtyard, providing a private and easily accessible space for outdoor dining, relaxing or enjoying a morning coffee. A small garden shed is positioned at the rear of the courtyard, providing useful additional storage. In addition, the property benefits from a separate parcel of garden situated just a few yards from the front door beside the reedbeds. This provides a further outdoor space in which to sit and enjoy the surroundings. The location is undoubtedly one of the home's defining features. For those looking for something genuinely individual, this is a rare opportunity to acquire a historic village home of considerable character and proportions, positioned right on the waterfront with spectacular views across the River Tavy. Bere Ferrers is an attractive waterside village situated on the Bere Peninsula between the Rivers Tavy and Tamar, surrounded by beautiful countryside and estuary scenery. The village has a strong sense of community and is a small village with a charming, old-fashioned pub which serves homemade food, railway station, café/shop and historic riverside church. There is a social club and a Saturday Market in the village hall where one can buy local produce. The unspoilt surroundings of the Tamar Valley with its rolling hills, meandering rivers and ancient woodlands are ideally suited to those who enjoy walking, riding and water sports and is ideal for sailing enthusiasts with a nearby sailing club and moorings. There are countryside walks and beautiful landscapes to admire within moments of leaving the door, including Dartmoor National Park, which is around 20 minutes by road. Perfect for those who enjoy being away from the bustle of modern life without being disconnected, Bere Ferrers benefits from its own railway station on the picturesque Tamar Valley Line. Bere Ferrers railway station is sited at the top of the village and goes directly into Plymouth within 20 minutes, then onto Exeter and in turn into London Paddington, which can be reached in around 4 hours. Situated 1.5 miles away is the village of Bere Alston which has a wide range of shopping facilities as well as a post office, doctors’ surgery, chemist, and a highly rated primary school. The village is situated approximately 6 miles from Tavistock and about 10 miles from Plymouth. There is a regular train service to and from Plymouth and a regular bus service to and from Tavistock. Situated on the desirable Hampstead Road in Brighton, this characterful property combines elegant period features with contemporary interiors, generous living spaces and a beautifully arranged rear garden. The street also benefits from convenient permit and paid parking options, with greater parking availability than many neighbouring roads, thanks to residential properties occupying just one side of the street. The property immediately impresses with its attractive period façade and welcoming entrance hallway, featuring original patterned floor tiles, decorative detailing and a staircase that sets the tone for the character found throughout. The ground floor offers two generous reception rooms, providing excellent flexibility for modern family living. The principal living room is a particularly impressive space, with a large bay window enjoying elevated views across Brighton, an attractive feature fireplace, bespoke shelving and ample room for both relaxing and dining. A second reception room provides an inviting additional living area, complete with a decorative fireplace, fitted shelving and French doors opening onto the courtyard, making it ideal as a family room, snug or entertaining space. To the rear, the spacious contemporary kitchen and dining room forms the heart of the home. Beautifully designed with sleek white cabinetry, contrasting worktops, a central island with breakfast bar seating and generous dining space, it offers the perfect setting for everyday family life and entertaining. Large sliding doors connect the kitchen to the courtyard, creating a wonderful flow between indoor and outdoor living and the ground floor cloakroom provides additional practicality. The first floor offers three well-proportioned bedrooms, each with its own individual character. The impressive bay-fronted principal bedroom on this floor enjoys elevated views, original wooden flooring and a beautiful period fireplace. An office (or additional bedroom) and a stylish family bathroom completes this floor. The second floor provides two further bedrooms and an additional bathroom, creating an excellent arrangement for growing families, guests or older children seeking their own space. The beautifully finished bathroom features a freestanding roll-top bath, separate shower, patterned flooring and elegant brass fittings. Throughout the property, a thoughtful combination of period charm and contemporary styling creates a home full of personality, with original fireplaces, decorative cornicing, large sash windows and carefully considered interiors. Outside, the property benefits from a delightful rear garden arranged across different levels, incorporating decked seating areas, established planting and space for outdoor dining and entertaining. The garden provides a wonderful retreat from city life, while the courtyard immediately adjoining the kitchen offers an additional outdoor seating area. Hampstead Road is a highly desirable residential address in Brighton, conveniently positioned for the independent shops, cafés and restaurants of Seven Dials, as well as Brighton Station and Preston Park Station (approx. 2 min walk), excellent local schools and the city centre. The nearby green spaces of Preston Park provide further appeal for families and those seeking an active outdoor lifestyle. Combining generous proportions, period elegance, contemporary living and a sought-after Brighton location, this exceptional family home offers a wonderful opportunity to enjoy the very best of city living.

A beautifully presented and wonderfully characterful Grade II listed two-bedroom home, enviably positioned at the top of Victoria Street within the highly sought-after Montpelier & Clifton Hill Conservation Area. Full of charm, warmth and individuality, this much-loved home has been exceptionally well cared for by the current owners and offers a rare combination of period character, beautifully maintained interiors and exceptional outside space. The accommodation is arranged over two floors and retains a wealth of charming period features, including elegant bow windows, original fireplaces, timber flooring and beautifully detailed interiors, while having been thoughtfully maintained to create a comfortable and inviting home. The impressive through lounge/dining room provides a wonderful heart to the home, with elegant proportions, a feature fireplace and bow window to the front, flowing through to the dining area at the rear and providing direct access to the garden. The well-appointed kitchen is positioned to the rear and is both practical and beautifully presented, with a good range of storage and worktop space. At the far end, a charming breakfast seating area creates an additional informal space for dining or relaxing, with views towards the garden. Upstairs are two well-proportioned bedrooms, with the principal bedroom enjoying the elevated outlook and sea views, alongside a stylish shower room. One of the property's most exceptional features is its outside space. The secluded patio garden is beautifully established and wonderfully private, providing a peaceful setting for outdoor dining and entertaining. Beyond this, and an extremely rare feature for a home of this type, is a separate roof terrace offering further space to sit and enjoy the elevated position and sea views. To have both a garden and a roof terrace in this location is a particularly unusual and desirable combination!. The property is situated in one of Brighton's most sought-after residential areas, within the Montpelier & Clifton Hill Conservation Area and close to the wealth of independent shops, cafés, restaurants and amenities of Seven Dials, Western Road and central Brighton. The seafront is also within easy reach, while Brighton Station is conveniently accessible for commuters. Offered for sale with no onward chain, this is a truly charming period home that combines character, excellent presentation and an exceptional selection of outside spaces in a highly desirable elevated location. Beautiful mid terrace home. Grade II listed. Roof terrace with sea views. Established rear garden. Through lounge/dining room. Two double bedrooms. Charming breakfast seating area. Full of natural light. Character & charm throughout. No onward chain

text: Situation. Braeface Farm is located outside the village of Neilston which is a popular commuter town to Glasgow with rail and car transport links. Neilston benefits from a co-op, fish and chip bar, bowling clubs, primary school, leisure centre and local churches. There are several outdoor pursuits on offer nearby with several country parks and woodlands ideal for walking or hacking. Harelaw Trout Fishery a popular spot for local anglers. As well as Fereneze, Paisley, East Renfrewshire golf clubs along the road. Newton Mearns is 7 miles to the East of the property and offers larger shops, restaurants, shopping centre and medical centre. Glasgow is Scotland’s largest city. Where there are several private schools for children of all ages in Glasgow which are within easy reach. Glasgow Airport and Prestwick Airport are 13 and 23 miles away respectively. Both Neilston and Dunlop have railway stations with regular connections to Glasgow and beyond. The Ayrshire coast is home to some exceptional yachting facilities with marinas in Troon, Largs, Inverkip, and Ardrossan. Description. Braeface Farmhouse offers an outstanding lifestyle amenity small holding with a large country house, stables, arena and grazing land extending to approximately 5.63 Ha (13.91 Acres) in total. Occupying an idyllic and private location, Braeface Farmhouse is a traditional stone built property under a pitched slate roof, with several chimney stacks, and finished with a white render. The house is finished to a high standard throughout with a traditional feel while retaining the warmth of a family home. The Kitchen is the heart of this home with ample worksurface and a range cooker, the large dining table is excellent for entertaining, while the sitting area adjoined is perfect to sit in and appreciate the view. The formal lounge is a magnificent room taking full advantage of the space on offer spanning 72m2, excellent for family parties or larger gatherings. The Family room is the cosiest room in the house with log burner on, perfect for enjoying some television. The sunroom connects the property with outside especially in the warmer weather. The principal room is located off the hall from the formal lounge, it enjoys a 27m² footprint, dual aspect allowing natural light in abundance, walk in closet and ensuite bathroom. The second bedroom is at the rear of the property with its own large dressing area, separate bathroom and dual aspect windows. Both upstairs bedrooms are doubles sharing a bathroom. The ground floor also benefits room a large storage room, W.C, utility and storage barn which also grants access to the car port. Garden. The property is set within a generous garden which extends to approximately 2 acres and is mostly laid to lawn enclosed by some shrubs and trees to the south and west. There is a large gravel driveway to the east of the property which provides ample space for parking vehicles. Buildings. The buildings at Braeface Farmhouse comprise:. Log store (9.50m x 8.30m). Of traditional stone construction under a pitched slate roof with a concrete floor. There is a small lean-to extension to the front of the building of timber and steel construction under a felt roof. Bothy (3.80m x 3.00m). Of stone construction under a pitched slate roof with a concrete floor. Additionally, there are equestrian facilities which are situated just to the north of the farmhouse, briefly they comprise:. Timber Stable Block (21.50m x 4.85m) + (7.33m x 4.85m). Of timber frame construction under a corrugated felt roof and a concrete floor. Accommodating 6 stables, tack room and feed stores. There is a turnout pen situated adjacent to the stable block. Outdoor Riding Arena. Adjacent to the stable block there is a riding arena with a sand surface enclosed with post and rail fencing. The Land. The land at Braeface Farmhouse extends to 4.84 Ha (11.96 Acres) and is split into two paddocks which are currently down to pasture and utilised for grazing livestock. The land is situated to the south of the farmhouse and is accessed via the main access road and a farm track. The land is predominately east facing and has been classified as being Grade 4.1 and 4.2 by the James Hutton Institute. The fields benefit from private source water supply. Method of sale. text: Significantly enhanced and beautifully presented throughout, this attractive two-bedroom end-terrace villa occupies a generous garden plot within a highly desirable pocket of Burnside. A particularly appealing feature of the property is its substantial south-facing rear garden, which enjoys an excellent degree of natural sunlight and provides an idyllic setting for outdoor relaxation and entertaining. The current owner has clearly taken great pride in the property, carrying out a number of thoughtful improvements which have brought a fresh and contemporary feel to the home while retaining its traditional character. Enhancements include replacement internal doors throughout, a stylishly refitted kitchen and bathroom, fresh crisp re-rendered exterior walls, together with an upgraded gas-fired central heating system. The property also benefits from double glazing. The result is a beautifully presented home, maintained in excellent order, with a pleasing finish both inside and out, offering an ideal opportunity for the next owner to move straight in and enjoy. The accommodation begins with a welcoming entrance hallway, with staircase leading to the upper floor. To the front, the lounge provides a comfortable and inviting reception space, enjoying a pleasant outlook and offering ample room for both relaxation and everyday living. To the rear, the well-appointed kitchen is fitted with a range of attractive storage units, complemented by a selection of integral appliances, creating a practical yet stylish workspace. A useful under-stair cupboard provides additional storage, while a door gives direct access to the rear garden. On the upper floor, a spacious landing gives access to two generously proportioned bedrooms, both offering excellent flexibility for a variety of furniture arrangements, alongside a beautifully appointed three-piece bathroom, finished in a contemporary style. A further noteworthy feature is the floored and lined attic room, accessed via a permanent staircase from the principal bedroom. This versatile additional space offers excellent potential for a variety of uses, whether as a home office, hobby room or valuable storage area. Externally, the property enjoys an attractive enclosed front garden, designed with ease of maintenance in mind, while to the rear lies a particularly impressive and expansive south-facing garden. Situated in the charming Oxfordshire hamlet of Taston, Lutleys and Blacksmiths Cottage represent a truly unique offering. For the first time in over half a century, these neighbouring period cottages are available together, presenting a remarkable opportunity to create an exceptional country home in a peaceful and highly sought-after setting. Believed to have been designed by the noted Victorian architect J.P. Seddon and formerly part of the Ditchley Estate, the cottages are steeped in local history and are even referenced in Pevsner's Guide to Oxfordshire. Surrounded by unspoilt countryside, they occupy a generous plot with mature gardens and a paddock and enjoy a wonderful sense of privacy and tranquillity. Lutleys benefits from a beautifully proportioned south-facing garden, while Blacksmiths enjoys attractive views across open farmland with woodland beyond. Both properties offer ample parking and extensive outdoor space, creating an enviable setting for family life or a countryside retreat. Planning permission has been granted for the sympathetic extension of both cottages, allowing buyers the opportunity to enhance and modernise the accommodation while preserving the character of the original buildings. Furthermore, ownership of both properties presents the exciting prospect of creating a single substantial residence, subject to the necessary consents. Combining architectural heritage, generous grounds and significant potential, this is an exceptionally rare opportunity to acquire two characterful period cottages in a peaceful and unspoilt rural setting. Rich in history yet offering considerable scope for enhancement, the properties provide an unusual chance from which to create a truly special country home. With mature gardens, far-reaching views across surrounding countryside and planning consent already in place, the combination of lifestyle, heritage and opportunity is particularly compelling. Set within one of Oxfordshire's most picturesque hamlets, opportunities of this nature are seldom available and are unlikely to be repeated for many years to come. Taston is a picturesque and peaceful hamlet surrounded by rolling Oxfordshire countryside, approximately four miles south of Chipping Norton. Offering a quintessential rural setting, it enjoys easy access to the town's excellent amenities, independent shops, restaurants and schooling, as well as the wider attractions of the Cotswolds. text: Your First Home, With Lower Running Costs in Mind! Modern Living, Solar Panels & an A-Rated EPC! The picturesque village of Cley-next-the-Sea is one of North Norfolk`s most iconic coastal locations, renowned for its rich history, charming flint cottages and thriving artistic community. Once a busy medieval port, Cley retains a strong sense of heritage, reflected in landmarks such as the historic Cley Windmill and the beautiful St Margaret`s Church, Cley. Today, it is highly regarded for its unspoilt character and relaxed coastal lifestyle. Amenities, History & Surrounding Area:. Cley offers a selection of boutique amenities including galleries, a village store, delicatessen and highly regarded places to eat, all contributing to its unique appeal. The surrounding marshes form part of the Cley Marshes Nature Reserve, one of the country`s most celebrated wildlife habitats, attracting birdwatchers and nature lovers alike. The wider coastline provides an array of scenic walks and beaches, while the nearby Georgian town of Holt offers further shopping, dining and schooling options. The village itself benefits from a strong community feel, with three churches in the wider setting and popular local pubs including the The Wiveton Bell and The Three Swallows both within walking distance. Quakers Garth offers a truly unique opportunity to take ownership of a beautifully appointed and much-loved family home. The property blends character features and modern comforts to create superb family accommodation situated in a position which makes the most of the stunning views of Coverdale whilst balancing its private location with accessibility to the village and its thriving community. DESCRIPTION The property is approached via a charming Green Lane leading from the eastern edge of the village. This short track provides a wonderful sense of privacy and opens into a generous parking area suitable for several vehicles. Entry is through a practical entrance lobby with bench seating and ample space for coats and boots, which in turn leads into the main hallway and access to the useful utility room. From the hallway, the accommodation flows into the heart of the home: an impressive open plan kitchen and dining space. Thoughtfully designed, this area features a striking garden room style extension that captures views over the garden and the stunning countryside beyond. The kitchen offers a modern, stylish layout with integrated appliances, a pantry and breakfast bar. The adjoining dining area enhances the sense of indoor/outdoor living, with direct access to the patio. The kitchen leads through to a welcoming living room with a multifuel burner and further garden views, and then on to a versatile family room. This flexible space can be adapted to suit individual needs and benefits from French windows as well as access to the potential annexe. Completing the ground floor is a storeroom/potential second kitchen, a cloakroom and a large double bedroom with ensuite and French windows directly into the garden. With its own independent entrance, this section of the property offers excellent potential as self-contained annexe, guest suite, or additional accommodation. The first floor is reached via the staircase from the hallway and leads to a central landing. Here you will find a family bathroom and three double bedrooms overlooking the gardens and far reaching views, including the dual aspect principal bedroom with ensuite. A further bedroom, currently used as a home office, enjoys views to the front and could serve as a large single or smaller double room. Externally, the property offers a substantial parking area to the front and beautifully landscaped gardens to the rear. The rear garden includes an attractive patio ideal for alfresco dining and entertaining, with sweeping views across Coverdale. Beyond this lies a generous lawn, productive vegetable garden, several sheds, and a standout Arctic BBQ cabin. Quakers Garth is a property of quality and character, appealing to buyers seeking a flexible, peaceful and desirable setting within the Yorkshire Dales National Park. Guide Price Range: £600,000 - £650,000. A Stunning Character Property. Well Appointed with High Quality Fixtures & Fittings. 4/5 Bedrooms. Open Plan Living. Beautiful Gardens & Patio. Potential Annexe. Stunning Views of Coverdale. Popular & Peaceful Village Location

Welcome… . Old Hall stands as a magnificent Grade II listed property, rich with history and brimming with character. As the current owners prepare to move on, a rare opportunity arises for a discerning buyer to become the next custodian of this remarkable home. Poised at the edge of Gayle, Old Hall welcomes visitors with its ornate moulded doorway, inscribed with the initials MAW, marking its 1695 origins and original owner, Matthew Weatherald. Mullioned windows add to the charm of this historic residence. Come on in… Step inside to a welcoming vestibule, its tiled floor and inset stone shelves perfectly suited for shedding muddy boots after a walk on the fells. The inner hallway stretches towards the rear of the property, awash with natural light from a window at its far end. To the right, a utility storage room features original stone shelving and a rugged stone-flagged floor. Continuing down the hallway, you’ll find the bathroom, thoughtfully appointed with a bath, separate shower, washbasin, and WC. This tranquil space offers a place to relax after days spent exploring the Dales. Lovely Living Spaces… The reception rooms grace the front of the property, where deep-set windows provide inviting perches to gaze out at the world beyond. The dining room has a beamed ceiling and elegant oak herringbone floors, offering ample space for a grand dining table fit for festive gatherings. Picture magical Christmas celebrations, with loved ones gathered around, savouring the year's most anticipated meal. A striking feature fireplace, flanked by built-in cupboards, anchors the room with character. The expansive living room centres on an impressive inglenook fireplace, where the wood-burning stove takes centre stage. Beamed ceilings and twin windows with inset seats overlook the front, creating a serene spot to unwind. Envision cosy winter evenings, curled up with a film or a good book by the roaring fire. Heart of the home… The kitchen, nestled at the rear of the property, opens directly to the garden. Traditional stone flags pave the floor, while shaker-style units with pristine white worktops offer abundant storage and workspace for culinary creativity. An inset porcelain Belfast sink adds a touch of rustic charm, and there's ample space for a range-style cooker. The breakfast bar offers a relaxed setting for morning coffee or casual conversation as meals are prepared. Beyond the kitchen lies a generous walk-in pantry with original stone shelving, a haven for the home cook. From here, a staircase leads to a practical first-floor storage area. Time for bed… Ascend the original stone staircase to the first floor, where four bedrooms await. The principal bedroom is generously proportioned and features two front-facing windows and a beamed ceiling. Off the landing, a door opens to a spacious storage area tucked beneath the eaves, with a second door providing access to steps leading down to the pantry below. The second bedroom features exposed ceiling beams and dual front-facing windows, one with a delightful arch that adds a unique touch of period character. A contemporary shower room features a walk-in cubicle clad in classic white metro tiles, inset shelving for toiletries, a sleek washbasin, and a WC. The design combines modern convenience with timeless style. Further along the corridor are two additional bedrooms, presently serving as separate study spaces. The smaller of the pair is distinguished by enchanting arched, mullioned windows, a subtle homage to the property’s heritage. Outside Step out through the kitchen's rear door into a private passageway, where an outdoor store leads to a secluded, sheltered courtyard. This tranquil oasis is perfect for morning coffee, with birdsong and the soothing sounds of a nearby waterfall. Stone steps lead up to a raised patio, ideal for alfresco dining, with space for a table and chairs. Two small outbuildings on the side of the property provide storage for coal and logs. The lawn rises gently behind the house, culminating at a vantage point from which the fells unfold over the rooftops. There is space to park a car at the front of the property, with additional parking available in the village. Out and about Gayle is a picturesque village on the outskirts of Hawes, where traditional stone cottages line the banks of Gayle Beck. The beck cascades through the heart of the village in a series of gentle waterfalls, flowing toward the landmark Gayle Mill and the distinctive pepperpot silhouette of Hawes church tower on the horizon. The recently restored mill stands as a testament to the village’s rich textile heritage, and many local homes were originally built for the workers who supported that legacy. Much of the village remains unchanged, preserving a timeless quality that makes it unique. As local historians Ella Pontefract and Marie Hartley observed, "Qualities which make for quaintness: hills rising above it, houses grouped around the beck, narrow alleys, a bridge, a mill, each so perfectly placed that a first view is startling." Few are as fortunate as those who can call this enchanting village their home. A Magnificent Home Filled With Character. Built In 1695 and Steeped In History. Quaint Village Location On The Outskirts Of Hawes. Spacious Living Rooms With Beamed Ceilings & Window Seats Overlooking The Village. While Away Days With The Sound Of The Nearby Waterfall An Ever-Present Background. 4 Beautiful Bedrooms. 2 Bathrooms. Lovely Kitchen With Separate Pantry. Tiered Gardens With Seating Areas, Lawn & 3 Outbuildings For Storage

The dining room is a generous and versatile room, ideal for both everyday family life and entertaining. Benefitting from a useful fitted cupboard and an excellent understairs storage cupboard, the room also provides access to the kitchen. Forming part of a later extension, the kitchen is fitted with a range of wall and base units and offers space for a freestanding cooker, washing machine and fridge freezer. A stainless steel sink is positioned beneath the rear-facing window, enjoying views over the delightful garden, whilst a wall-mounted boiler and external door complete this practical space. Offering an abundance of potential, character and charm, this attractive home presents a wonderful opportunity to acquire a well-cared-for property in a sought-after location, ready for its next chapter and new custodians to make it their own. text: 29 Main Street offers a very exciting opportunity to purchase a two bedroom character cottage which has been subject to a comprehensive scheme of renovation, set in this central position within the sought after village of Embsay. There is also the rare addition of a spacious rear garden and a barn which is set over three floors, suitable for a variety of uses, especially those looking to create a workshop or an annex for the cottage. Fitted with sealed unit UPVC glazing, gas fired central heating and high quality fixtures and fittings throughout, the property comprises briefly:. An entrance hall, a study/dining room, a cosy living room with a feature stone fireplace and a beautiful newly fitted kitchen with modern fitted wall and base units and brand new integrated appliances. To the first floor there are two good sized double bedrooms, one of which (the larger) has bespoke fitted wardrobes and the house bathroom which is fitted with a contemporary three piece suite. The other benefit to the first floor is that gas fired underfloor heating has been fitted. Outside to the rear of the property is a spacious garden which is mainly cobbled with a tiered lawn area, a small herb garden, a timber storage shed and potential to purchase further garden area (subject to agreement with relevant parties). There is also the rare addition of a barn which is set over three floors with part of the ground floor used as a garage and having power and lighting throughout, the barn offers an exclusive opportunity for buyers to have their own workshop area or to create an annex for the cottage. Guide Price £260,000 - £290,000. 22 Hargill is a spacious detached bungalow, situated in the sought-after village of Harmby. Harmby is a popular and peaceful Dales village with a strong community spirit, conveniently situated just a mile from Leyburn, with the neighbouring village of Spennithorne also close by. Both villages offer a range of community and recreational facilities, while Leyburn provides an excellent selection of independent shops, cafés, pubs, restaurants, professional and medical services. Surrounded by beautiful countryside, the area offers superb opportunities for walking and exploring the Yorkshire Dales, with the market towns of Richmond and Bedale also within easy reach. The accommodation offers a good-sized living room, a well-proportioned kitchen, three bedrooms and a family bathroom. A useful garden room provides additional living or dining space and enjoys views over the garden. There is also a large attached garage, incorporating a built-in utility area and separate WC, providing excellent practical space for storage, laundry and household requirements. The property benefits from efficient oil-fired central heating. Externally, the property benefits from attractive wraparound gardens which are a particular feature of the home. The gardens are well established, with a good selection of mature shrubs, raised beds and lawned areas, creating a pleasant and private outdoor space. The elevated position provides lovely views across the surrounding countryside and towards the hills beyond. A private driveway provides off-road parking for two vehicles and leads to the garage. The bungalow is now in need of updating and modernisation, but offers a particularly good opportunity for a purchaser looking to improve and personalise a property to their own taste and requirements. While the accommodation is well proportioned and perfectly usable in its current form, the kitchen, bathroom, windows and general décor would benefit from modernisation, allowing the new owner to introduce a more contemporary style and potentially improve the layout and finish where desired. The underlying space, gardens, views and location provide an excellent foundation for creating a very comfortable and appealing home. 22 Hargill therefore represents an excellent opportunity to acquire a spacious detached bungalow in a highly desirable village location, with well-proportioned accommodation, efficient oil central heating, attractive wraparound gardens, lovely countryside views and considerable potential for modernisation and improvement. A generously proportioned and characterful dales cottage dating from circa 1690 and offering well balanced three double bedroom accommodation with two reception rooms and a welcoming hall. The location is just 5 miles from the many amenities available in Sedbergh, junction 37 of the M6 is within easy reach and the market town of Kirkby Lonsdale is 10 miles away. Property Overview: Built in circa 1690, Church Gate Cottage as the name suggests, is located next to the village church of St Andrew's right in the heart of the village. Improved and updated over the years, the cottage has the benefit of the charm and character of its era blending with modern day comforts of double glazing, brand new central heating boiler and recently installed Hyco electric hot water boiler. Stepping inside, a warm welcome awaits those that view with original flagged flooring, exposed timbers and stone work all showcased in the generous entrance hall; great as a second dining or living space for entertaining friends and family with access into the ground floor living spaces, along with a stone staircase that leads up to the first floor. There is also a handy under the stairs cupboard. The sitting room to the left of the hallway is full of charm with a bay window overlooking the cobble street to the front and two side windows enjoying distant fell views. To complete the character of the room is the open fireplace and a wealth of exposed beams and stonework. The dining room overlooks the church yard to the rear as does the breakfast kitchen, and a cloakroom just off the dining room offers that all important downstairs WC. The breakfast kitchen has two windows both with deep sills and is fitted with a range of wall and base units with complementary working surfaces and a single drainer stainless steel sink. There is a slot in oven and fridge freezer, along with a washing machine. Upstairs opening off the landing are three double bedrooms, bathroom and useful storage cupboard, with bedroom one having an original oak door. All the bedrooms enjoy delightful aspects of village life and distant views. The bathroom has a window, part tiled walls and a radiator and heated towel rail to warm the room. A four piece suite comprises a panel bath with tiled splash back, a panelled shower cubicle with Mira shower, pedestal wash hand basin and WC.
